summary: Every fixture under this directory was written for this test. No file is copied from another repository. Each document is a tools/list result with one tool (name, description, inputSchema), the client-visible fields of ShenyuToolDefinition; requestConfig is server-side and is not part of the client-visible contract, so it is not included.

sections.note: The number spelling differs, the value does not. The 4.50, 1E30 and 2e-3 cases are the section 3.2.2 sample literals; 1.0 and -0 follow from section 3.2.2.3, which defers to ECMA-262 Number::toString. appendix-b carries the 24 rows of Appendix B that have a canonical form.

JSON numbers are IEEE 754 doubles here; 9007199254740993 (2^53 + 1) is not representable and is held as 9007199254740992. The expected canonical literal is pinned to 9007199254740992; a parser that keeps arbitrary precision would write 9007199254740993 and fail this case on purpose.

The 32 control characters U+0000..U+001F (short escapes for U+0008, U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, U+000D, lowercase \u00hh otherwise), quotation mark, reverse solidus, U+007F, U+20AC and U+1F600 as raw UTF-8, and the solidus unescaped (from the section 3.2.2 sample).
The section 3.2.3 sorting test data as property names; members sort by UTF-16 code units.
An ASCII tools/list descriptor whose members are reordered at three levels: different raw bytes, the same canonical bytes (no canonical descriptor drift).
A real schema change (include_lines becomes required). The canonical bytes differ, which shows the canonicalizer does not hide drift.

expected_bytes_source.description: The expected canonical literals are taken from the text of RFC 8785 and written into the fixtures as text; they are not produced by the test-scoped canonicalizer. The fixtures were independently cross-checked against a separate JavaScript JCS implementation.

rfc8785_sections.literals: string escaping: \b \t \n \f \r, lowercase \u00hh for the other control characters, quotation mark and reverse solidus escaped, everything else (U+007F, U+20AC, U+1F600) as is
number serialization as ECMA-262 Number::toString of the IEEE 754 double: 1.0 -> 1, -0 -> 0, 1e-7, and 2^53+1 held as 9007199254740992
member sorting by UTF-16 code units: the seven-key sorting test data, and the empty key before "a", "aa", "ab"
the 24 rows of the IEEE 754 number table that have a canonical form

sidecars: Each before/after file has a .sha256 sidecar holding the SHA-256 of its canonical bytes; each .canonical.json file holds those canonical bytes with no trailing newline, and its sidecar is the SHA-256 of the file, as in shenyu-admin/src/test/resources/app-auth.

complements.relation: These fixtures complement the ChangeProof pilot package and do not repeat it: its cases (a field made required, an output enum widened, an annotation-only change, allOf/not as indeterminate, and an ASCII key-order control) are not re-created here. This directory adds the RFC 8785 number, string-escaping and Unicode key-order rules that the ASCII key-order control does not exercise.
complements.license_note: The ChangeProof tree does not name a license, so none of its files are copied into this Apache-licensed repository; it is referenced by URL only.

not_included.reason: RFC 8785 section 3.2.2.2 requires an error, not a canonical form; it is a rejection case, not a before/after pair, and Java JSON parsers differ on whether they accept it at parse time.
A parse-time rejection (I-JSON), not a canonicalization rule; there is no canonical form to compare. The test parser rejects duplicates.
Not JSON numbers; RFC 8785 Appendix B lists them as errors, with no canonical form.

scope: Canonical equality shows identical canonical bytes only. It is not schema-semantic equivalence, it is not a compatibility verdict, and it says nothing about runtime pinning, generation consistency or authorization scope.
